extracted.intended_audience: prospective Chinese high school contestants, coaches, and educators interested in the Chinese Mathematical Olympiad
extracted.subtask_description: Information and procedural standards for entry, exam format, scoring, awards, and selection to the national training squad for the Chinese Mathematical Olympiad (CMO). Useful for students, coaches, and organizers preparing for or administering the CMO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (provincial qualification)
rubrics_metrics.description: To take part in the Chinese Mathematical Olympiad, high school students have to attain top positions in their own provinces in the National High School Mathematics Interprovincial Competition (全国高中数学联合竞赛), which is held on the second Sunday of September each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provincial mathematics societies often hold preliminary tests to pre-select students for the National High School Mathematics Competition, although these tests do not constitute a part of the official IMO team selection process. Based on results each province is allocated a quota to enter the CMO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quota allocation per province
rubrics_metrics.description: Each province is allocated a quota to enter the Chinese Mathematical Olympiad based on results of the National High School Mathematics Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In early editions quotas were usually 3 to 5 per province but could be higher for strong provinces (e.g., up to 15). Quotas have increased; the 2023 CMO quotas ranged from 6 to 26, totalling about 550 contestants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional invitation categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Also invited to the CMO are past national training squad members who are still in high schools, and around 15 of the top contestants in the China Girls Mathematical Olympiad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supplements province-allocated quotas to include selected individuals from other recognized programs or past squads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants (teams represented)
rubrics_metrics.description: Its participants are teams of high school students from every province of mainland China, as well as guest teams from the two special administrative regions Hong Kong and Macau, and also from Russia and Singapore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMO functions as a national-level invitational with invited guest teams allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format (exam structure and schedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chinese Mathematical Olympiad follows the same format as the IMO. Two papers are set, each with 3 problems. The examination is held on two consecutive mornings, and contestants have 4 hours and 30 minutes each day to work on the 3 problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure mirrors IMO: two 3-problem papers on consecutive days with long-form proof-style problems; time per paper is 4.5 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring system and problem value
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chinese Mathematical Olympiad is graded in 3-point increments, so that each problem is worth 21 points, making the total score 126, triple that of the IMO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring increments and per-problem maximum are fixed: 0–21 in steps of 3 points per problem; total sum across six problems equals 126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chinese Mathematical Olympiad has first, second and third class awards. There is also an award for the best team called "Chern Shiing-Shen Cup".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medal/award tiers are grouped into classes rather than named medals; team award named for Shiing-Shen Chern.

rubrics_metrics.name: National training squad invitation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, about 60 highest-scoring contestants amongst the first class award winners are invited to the national training squad, who will go through a training camp to select the IMO team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitation is based on being among the top first-class winners; approximate squad size ~60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training camp selection process (pre-2017)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until 2016, the training camp consisted of a single phase with several regular tests and a team selection test, which was in the format of the IMO. The IMO team was selected based on the final result, of which both the regular tests and the team selection test were worth 50%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection combined cumulative performance across regular tests and a final team-selection test equally (50/50).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training camp selection process (since 2017)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2017, the training camp has been split into two phases, held in two separate periods at two high schools. In each phase of the training camp that lasts for about 8 to 9 days, two team selection tests, each of the same format as the IMO, are conducted. In the first phase, 15 top scoring members are selected to the next phase, and at the end of the second phase, the six IMO team members are selected based on the total points of the four team selection tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is now based on aggregate performance across four IMO-format team selection tests (two per phase); a first cut to 15 after phase one, final six chosen by total points.

rubrics_metrics.name: University admission privilege for national training squad members
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the national training squad have guaranteed admission to any universities in China without sitting the Gaokao examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being in the national training squad confers a major educational advantage (exemption from national university entrance exam).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of CMO in IMO selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chinese Mathematical Olympiad is part of the selection process for the Chinese team to the International Mathematical Olympiad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance at CMO (and subsequent national training camp/tests) is a key input into choosing the IMO team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting and venue practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chinese Mathematical Olympiad used to be held in universities. Since 2002 (except in 2004), the CMO has been held in high schools to let the high schools take on a more active role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change of venue policy was motivated by university recruitment tensions; default hosting preference is high schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational adjustments during COVID-19
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the outbreak of the COVID-19 epidemic in early 2020, the training camp was not held and the Chinese team for the 2020 IMO was selected based on the scores of the 2019 CMO. The 2022 CMO was moved to a virtual event with contestants competing in the exam centers of their own provinces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contingency rules: when camps/exams cannot be held normally, selection may rely on previous-year scores or virtual administration.
